acceptanceCriteria: The trigger for the slow path is identified with file:line and reproduced in a test or scale harness with concurrent writers.
Under concurrent writer activity at about 22.5k receipts, plain reads stay within a stated bound (target under 1 s warm) or the remaining cost is explained with evidence.
No read writes state (invariant 4); stale or forged derived state still falls back to full verification.
The reporter's two questions are answered on the GitHub issue.
body: GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#707 (2026-10-09), on installed main-02e8457 (1.0.0-rc.2) with about 22.5k receipts, 4 pool members and 3-7 dispatcher workers. Three concurrent plain reads (queue status, ticket show) launched by tooling ran 1-2 min at about 48% CPU each. sample shows internal/tasks/wire parsing ((*parser).str, checkHostile, appendString); lsof shows receipts/, requests/, attempts/ and evidence/ held open. The same commands by hand in the same window took 0.17-0.26 s. Suspected: reads fall off the checkpoint/snapshot path into a full journal replay or verification when the head moves during an active writer pool, and each concurrent reader replays independently. Questions from the reporter: what triggers the fallback, does the CTS-V0-006 2 s re-read budget bound it, and can concurrent cold readers share work or wait for the writer checkpoint. Related: #446, #641, V1-1051, V1-1053.
